horizon_driver: Genuinely bimodal within this merged actor: NBIM/GIC operate on a generational, sponsor-state-wealth-preservation mandate (the longest horizon in the system, per the Cartographer); PIF now operates on a much shorter, Vision-2030-linked political-delivery clock (effectively 4-6 years) because of active fiscal pressure on its sponsor state — this internal split is itself a key 2026 finding.

stated_vs_revealed.stated: PIF has historically framed itself as Saudi Arabia's 'global investment powerhouse,' targeting a rising share of assets deployed abroad as part of Vision 2030 diversification.
stated_vs_revealed.revealed: PIF's new 2026-2030 strategy explicitly cuts international allocation from a peak of roughly 30% down to 20%, targets 80% domestic investment of its ~$925bn portfolio, and has already implemented a minimum 20% (up to 60% on individual projects) spending cut across more than 100 portfolio companies and giga-projects, with PIF's own equity contribution to new projects falling from 70-100% toward a 30-40% target as the balance shifts to GCC private capital, FDI partners, and subsidiary IPOs.
stated_vs_revealed.delta: PIF's self-image as a 'global sovereign investor with a multi-decade horizon' is currently false in practice. Lower oil revenue and giga-project cost overruns have forced a hard reversal toward a shorter-horizon, domestic fiscal-support role for its sponsor state — the opposite of the Cartographer's generic 'longest-horizon capital actor' framing for this whole tier.

stated_vs_revealed.stated: Sovereign funds broadly claim diversified, risk-managed portfolios appropriate to their stated long investment horizon (standard SWF governance language).
stated_vs_revealed.revealed: NBIM ($2.2T, world's largest) holds roughly 40% in US equities with concentrated single-name mega-cap stakes (1.3% of Nvidia, 1.2% of Apple, 1.3% of Microsoft), while Temasek is raising its AI portfolio weight from 6% (Q1 2026) toward a 15%-by-2031 target, and Temasek plus GIC together closed 13 AI-related deals in the first half of 2026 alone (including Anthropic, OpenAI, and Supabase). NBIM's own internal 'AI correction' stress-test scenario shows a hypothetical 53% equity drawdown cutting total fund value by 35% — i.e., the fund quantifies this concentration risk internally while remaining fully exposed to it.
stated_vs_revealed.delta: The largest, most credible members of this 'diversified, patient' tier are converging on a shared, correlated thematic bet (US mega-cap AI) at the same time. This is a systemic exposure across the SWF tier as a whole, not diversification away from tail risk, and it is the clearest concrete evidence for the Cartographer's 'horizon arbitrage' framing turning into a correlated crowding trade.

tripwires.if: a broad AI-equity correction exceeds roughly 20%
tripwires.then: NBIM-style funds absorb large marked losses but do not divest at the bottom, per stated rebalancing-not-panic governance — directly testable against NBIM's own published 'AI correction' scenario model

tripwires.if: Saudi oil revenue falls further or the fiscal breakeven price rises
tripwires.then: PIF's domestic allocation share rises further still — treat the 80/20 target as a floor under further fiscal stress, not a ceiling

tripwires.if: a G7/US jurisdiction restricts SWF ownership of AI or critical-tech firms on national-security grounds
tripwires.then: Gulf and Chinese SWFs redirect strategic stakes toward non-US venues (Europe, Asia) as the primary substitution channel

what_would_change_my_mind: PIF returning to a rising international-allocation share would falsify the 'short-horizon fiscal-support vehicle' reading of it specifically. Sustained improvement in CIC disclosure would allow a real credibility read for that member rather than an inferred one — currently flagged low-confidence for CIC specifically.
